newsitem.title: USA: AMR sets retail value of jet deal at $6.5 bln.
newsitem.headline: AMR sets retail value of jet deal at $6.5 bln.

text.p: AMR Corp said Thursday its firm order for 103 Boeing Co aircraft has a retail value of about $6.5 billion.
AMR Chairman Robert Crandall declined to disclose exactly how much the airline would pay but said "You can count on the fact that we bought them for a few dollars less than that."
AMR also has purchase rights for an additional 527 Boeing jets, ranging from 737 to 777 models.
Under the unique purchase right agreement, AMR and Boeing have set the price that AMR will pay for each jet, but the airline can tailor the aircraft delivery schedule to match its growth needs.
The purchase rights deal allows AMR to acquire the planes at a set price with as little as 15 months' notice.
Typically, airlines have "options" to buy aircraft that are exercisable 24-36 months prior to delivery. Once this time period passes, the options and the price terms expire.
AMR said it did not pay for the "rights" to buy the planes with as little as 15 months' notice.
"We are not paying for anything. We are effectively getting those purchase rights in exchange for giving Boeing an exclusive as our aircraft provider," Crandall said.
Boeing will be American's exclusive jet provider through the year 2018.
Boeing cannot book orders for the purchase rights until the orders are confirmed, AMR said.
